text:
The Bruins' worst moment of Friday wasn't the 3-1 loss to Toronto. It was David Pastrnak leaving with a lower-body injury, per Daily Faceoff. Until there's word on him, that is the story of Boston's season, because the top line of Pastrnak, Pavel Zacha and JJ Peterka has been their engine: 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) together and a 9-5 goal edge.

Step back and Boston is in good shape, 15-9-1 with 31 points and a 73% playoff chance by our simulations. The honest version is that the record runs a bit ahead of the play. The Bruins have 50.5% of the expected goals overall; they've scored about six more than their chances suggest and allowed about nine fewer, which is a lot of goaltending. That goaltending is wobbling. Jeremy Swayman has drawn a run of unflattering headlines and allowed three on 18 shots Friday, while Michael DiPietro has been the hot hand, .926 over his last five starts.

The best news has been the defence: Hampus Lindholm and Charlie McAvoy own 64% of the expected goals together. Elias Lindholm's four-goal night against Washington changed the conversation about his contract. And Zacha's name keeps coming up in the Wild's search for a centre. They are 5-5 in their last ten. Watch Pastrnak's status, and the net.
